scope.summary: Add a planning/spec-only architecture artifact for compliance-selective cell placement, keeping compliance-heavy controls scoped to regulated tenant sub-scopes while ordinary workloads remain on lean standard cells.
explicit_non_claims: No product code, runtime placement, API, CLI, generated face, or oya/cloud reorg mutation is introduced.
No compliance readiness, certification, provider eligibility, or regulator approval is claimed.
ADR-0248 and ADR-0251 remain Proposed/planning-impact context only; this artifact does not elevate them into binding merge authority.

facets.F1_correctness: The plan covers standard vs compliant cell classes, CDE/KYC/identity placement, per-pack control elevation, shared-responsibility evidence, cost/freshness models, migration gates, and fail-closed placement constraints.
facets.F2_tests: Focused acceptance checks assert the required REGCLOUD-001 terms and source path references; markdown diff hygiene is checked with git diff --check.
facets.F3_maintainability: The artifact is isolated under plan/ and explicitly scopes downstream implementation notes into separate future Kanban cards.
facets.F4_compatibility: The artifact composes existing tenant, compliance-pack, DR-floor, ADR-0240, ADR-0248, and ADR-0251 context without changing schemas or runtime behavior.
facets.F5_security: The placement rules deny non-compliant fallback, prevent raw CDE/KYC/identity-sensitive leakage into standard cells, and require fresh provider/certification evidence before regulated placement.
facets.F6_privacy: Regulated personal, health, identity, and jurisdiction-scoped data are modeled as sub-scope/compliant-cell placements with redacted projections to standard cells.
facets.F7_operability: The plan defines migration gates, failure-mode responses, evidence packets, stale-certification behavior, and Tier 2 snapshot authority boundaries.
facets.F8_performance: The cost model keeps standard workloads lean and applies compliant-cell costs only after eligibility constraints pass, preserving hot-path intra-cell serving.
facets.F9_compliance: Pack activation narrows behavior through strictest-rule-wins control vectors, DR floors, provider residency evidence, and audit-chain evidence packets.
facets.F10_reversibility: The change is a documentation/spec planning artifact and can be reverted without data or runtime migration.
facets.F11_observability: The plan requires placement-decision evidence rows, shared-responsibility packets, audit-chain emissions, and freshness/cost attributes for future implementation.
facets.F13_migration: The plan separates standard-to-compliant, compliant-to-standard, certification-expiry/provider-loss, and capacity-rebalance gates with explicit rollback and evidence semantics.
facets.A1_naming_adherence: The plan uses the REGCLOUD-001 card identifier and repo-relative plan path.
facets.A2_documentation_adherence: Frontmatter records lane, scope, owner, related ADRs, source specs, and the non-mutating blast radius.
facets.A3_structure_adherence: The document is organized as goal/non-goals, cell classes, inputs, algorithm, workload matrix, control elevation, evidence, cost, freshness, migration, gates, failure modes, and acceptance checklist.
facets.A4_architecture_adherence: The architecture preserves cells as the blast-radius primitive and Tier 2 as authoritative for tenancy/cell/pack metadata while Tier 3 serves from signed snapshots.
facets.A5_dependency_adherence: No dependency, CLI, runtime, generated face, or schema change is introduced.
facets.A6_schema_adherence: The artifact cites existing schemas/specs but does not mutate them; future machine-readable placement contracts are explicitly deferred.
facets.A7_algorithm_adherence: The placement algorithm evaluates hard constraints before scoring, applies deny-wins, narrows elevation to sub-scopes, and shuffle-shards only within eligible pools.
